PullRequest.Title: extensions: add delayed auto-update mode to extensions.autoUpdate
PullRequest.Body:
## What

Folds a **6-hour delayed auto-update** mode into the existing `extensions.autoUpdate` setting. The setting is now a string enum and is policy-controllable.

- `extensions.autoUpdate`: `'on' | 'delayed' | 'off'` (was a boolean / `onlyEnabledExtensions` enum)
  - **On** – enabled extensions update automatically.
  - **Delayed** – enabled extensions update automatically, but only 6 hours after a new version is published.
  - **Off** – extensions are not updated automatically.
- Made the setting policy-controllable via the `ExtensionsAutoUpdate` policy.

## Behavior in `delayed` mode

- An extension whose newer version was published **less than 6 hours ago** is treated as *outdated-but-delayed*:
  - excluded from auto-update,
  - excluded from the Extensions activity badge,
  - surfaces an **info status** explaining that it is not yet auto updated and when it will be (relative time, refreshed on hover).
- **Manual updates still work** regardless of the delay.
- The "Enable/Disable Auto Update for All Extensions" actions are hidden when the setting is policy-controlled.

## Migration

Startup migration of legacy values plus defensive read-time normalization in `getAutoUpdateValue()`:

- `true` / `'all'` / `'onlyEnabledExtensions'` -> `'on'`
- `false` / `'none'` / `'onlySelectedExtensions'` -> `'off'`
- `'delayed'` -> `'delayed'`

## Tests

Added unit tests in `extensionsWorkbenchService.test.ts` covering `getAutoUpdateValue()` normalization, `isAutoUpdateDelayed()` boundaries, and `getAutoUpdateDelayRemaining()`; updated plugin auto-update/marketplace tests for the new enum values.

## Notes for reviewers

- `build/lib/policies/policyData.jsonc` still needs to be regenerated via `npm run export-policy-data` (the `ExtensionsAutoUpdate` policy enum/enumDescriptions changed) — blocked locally by a corrupted Electron install, so it needs a regen by a codeowner/CI.
- Validated with `compile-check-ts-native`, `valid-layers-check`, and hygiene. Unit tests could not be executed locally (corrupted Electron) but compile clean.


Fixes - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/7834, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/7769

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed gate, legacy-value migration, event batching, absence of coalescing, and full-inventory gallery call are all directly visible in the traced code. Exact request latency and how often users toggle extensions vary, but the added network mechanism and O(installed extensions) payload per event are unambiguous.
Findings.PerformanceResource: marketplace network requests plus request/response bytes and per-extension metadata processing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N installed extensions and E separate enablement events, the new path performs E network requests each carrying/processing O(N) extension metadata; because calls are fire-and-forget, closely spaced events can overlap rather than coalesce.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive network I/O and avoidable CPU/serialization work, with concurrent requests able to reduce responsiveness and throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, the default legacy value `true` did not satisfy the `=== 'onlyEnabledExtensions'` gate, so enabling an extension did not trigger this full-gallery refresh. Only users explicitly configured for `onlyEnabledExtensions` paid this cost.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Extension enablement events in both `'on'` and `'delayed'` modes now call `checkForUpdates`, instead of doing so only for the former `'onlyEnabledExtensions'` mode. `checkForUpdates` enumerates every installed extension and sends the complete list to `galleryService.getExtensions`; calls are neither debounced nor protected by an in-flight promise.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1142 changes the gate from `getAutoUpdateValue() === 'onlyEnabledExtensions'` to `getAutoUpdateValue() !== 'off'`; the same PR maps legacy/default `true` to `'on'` at extensions.contribution.ts:2139, so the default population newly reaches `checkForUpdates` on enablement events.
Findings.Title: Coalesce update checks after extension enablement
Findings.Impact: With the default auto-update setting, enabling one extension now causes a background marketplace request for metadata for every installed extension; enabling several extensions separately can launch overlapping requests. On profiles with many extensions or a slow/enterprise marketplace this creates avoidable network traffic, serialization/response processing, and contention immediately after each enable action.
Findings.Evidence: `initializeAutoUpdate` subscribes directly to `extensionEnablementService.onEnablementChanged` and invokes `checkForUpdates` without awaiting, debouncing, or reusing an in-flight call. `ExtensionEnablementService.setEnablement` emits one event per command (including recursively enabled dependencies/packs), while separate commands emit separate events. `checkForUpdates` at lines 1976-2020 rebuilds `infos` from all `this.local` entries and calls the network-backed `galleryService.getExtensions(infos, ...)`. Thus rapid separate enable actions can overlap full-inventory marketplace requests.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the newly enabled-extension semantics without querying the whole inventory per event: coalesce enablement events behind a single in-flight/debounced check and, preferably, pass only the newly enabled extension infos to the existing batched `galleryService.getExtensions` path before syncing those results.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The timer-to-network call path and rescheduling loop are explicit, and `checkForUpdates` demonstrably enumerates the full installed collection. The number of staggered updates varies by profile, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: marketplace requests, request/response bytes, and CPU work for all installed extension metadata
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N installed extensions and D distinct delayed-update publication deadlines, the timer path performs up to D full O(N) marketplace checks during the six-hour window rather than refreshing only the candidates whose deadline expired.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive network I/O and repeated serialization/metadata processing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no per-publication deadline timer; stable builds used one grouped update check on the existing 12-hour schedule (and eligible Insider builds used the existing 1-hour schedule), so staggered extension publication times did not add full-inventory checks.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Delayed mode records the earliest remaining publication delay and, at every expiry, starts a complete update check for all installed extensions. After the eligible extension is handled, any other delayed extension with a later publication timestamp schedules another complete check.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 2251 newly schedules `eventuallyCheckForUpdates(true)` for `soonestDelayRemaining`; that helper immediately calls full `checkForUpdates()` and then `autoUpdateExtensions` schedules the next remaining deadline.
Findings.Title: Limit delayed-deadline checks to eligible extensions
Findings.Impact: When several installed extensions have updates published at different times within the six-hour window, VS Code issues a full marketplace metadata request at each distinct deadline, even though only the extension(s) reaching that deadline need refreshing. Profiles with many installed extensions therefore incur repeated large background requests and metadata processing throughout the delay window.
Findings.Evidence: `autoUpdateExtensions` computes the minimum positive delay over `this.outdated`, sets this timer, and returns when nothing is eligible. The callback reaches `eventuallyCheckForUpdates(true)`, which cancels the periodic delayer and immediately awaits `checkForUpdates`; that method serializes all installed extension infos and calls `galleryService.getExtensions`. Gallery synchronization invokes `eventuallyAutoUpdateExtensions` again, which installs mature entries and schedules the next distinct deadline. No grouping window or candidate subset prevents repeated all-installed queries.
Findings.Recommendation: At a deadline, refresh only the delayed extension IDs whose eligibility time has arrived using the existing batched `galleryService.getExtensions` API, then sync/install those results and schedule the next deadline. Coalesce nearby deadlines so one targeted request serves the group while preserving the check for a newer published version.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup, policy initialization, and legacy setting migration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration registration and migration occur during workbench startup. The new policy context performs one synchronous configuration inspection in the contribution constructor; no network work was added to this startup path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Normalize and persist a legacy configuration value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one persisted value migration for the `extensions.autoUpdate` key per affected profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing migration only rewrote `onlySelectedExtensions`; the PR broadens the one-key normalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A one-time configuration persistence operation may occur during migration, but it does not scale with installed extensions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One auto-update configuration value per profile.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single startup initialization; subsequent policy-context updates are event-driven and synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values are served by the configuration service; migration is a one-time normalization of the stored key. The policy context reads `inspect()` and then updates only when that key changes. No collection cache is added or invalidated on startup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration, migration, and context initialization are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact configuration persistence timing is implementation-dependent, but cardinality is fixed at one key.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup work is constant-sized and the only persistence is a one-time migration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enabling extensions with auto-update set to the migrated default `'on'` or new `'delayed'` mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The check is fire-and-forget after the enablement event, so extension enablement itself need not await it, but its network, serialization, and response processing contend with foreground work immediately afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query compatible marketplace metadata for the complete installed extension set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One marketplace request per enablement event, each containing all N installed eligible extension infos; E separate events produce E requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy/default `true` did not pass the old `=== 'onlyEnabledExtensions'` gate, so this request was absent for default users; only the explicitly selected legacy mode triggered it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the logical enablement critical path but concurrent with the post-enable user workflow and capable of consuming network/CPU resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed extensions and E distinct enablement events after event-level batching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One enable-all command emits one batched event, including recursively enabled dependencies/packs. Separate rapid enable commands emit separate events, and direct `checkForUpdates` calls can overlap because there is no debounce or in-flight promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `checkForUpdates` does not cache or coalesce an in-flight gallery request. Each enablement event rebuilds the full installed-extension info list and queries the marketplace again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed gate, `true` to `'on'` migration, event emission, all-installed enumeration, and network call were all traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Profiles vary in installed-extension count, marketplace latency, and frequency of separate enable actions; these affect severity, not the proven added request path.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the PR materially broadens an uncoalesced full-inventory marketplace query to the default population.

Scenarios.Scenario: Delayed auto-update eligibility as multiple extension versions mature
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At each six-hour eligibility deadline, the timer immediately schedules a marketplace check; that check must finish before gallery synchronization can re-run auto-update and install the now-eligible update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh marketplace metadata for every installed extension when the earliest delayed update matures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one full installed-set request for each distinct delayed publication deadline D; each request carries/processes N installed extension infos.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-publication deadline checks existed; stable used the existing 12-hour grouped poll and eligible Insider builds used the existing 1-hour poll.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The full query is on the path to installing each matured delayed update; unrelated extension metadata inflates that path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install boundary per eligible extension after the query, unchanged in shape and intentionally delayed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible auto-updates were already installed per extension after a periodic gallery check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to complete the update after eligibility; the finding concerns the unrelated full inventory refresh before it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed extensions and D distinct update publication timestamps within the delay window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The delayed timer itself holds only one soonest deadline and uses the shared periodic delayer, so its own checks are serial. Distinct publication deadlines are processed sequentially as D full checks; unrelated direct `checkForUpdates` callers are not globally coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current gallery metadata remains attached to each extension, but the deadline callback deliberately runs a fresh gallery query. No candidate subset or deadline-group cache limits that refresh to extensions whose delay expired.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: minimum-delay scheduling, immediate full check, gallery synchronization, and next-deadline rescheduling are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: D depends on how many installed extensions receive staggered updates in a six-hour window; exact request size and duration vary by gallery and profile.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: each staggered deadline repeats collection-wide network work that can be targeted and coalesced while preserving latest-version validation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hovering extension list rows to refresh delayed-update relative time
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed hover provider awaits `recomputeStatus()` before returning markdown, placing status CPU work on hover display. Cached asynchronous checks resolve without a repeated boundary request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load gallery policy manifest or an extension manifest for status evaluation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one gallery-manifest initialization globally and one extension-manifest request per Extension object on a cold cache; the pre-existing initial status computation already triggers these where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same status action computed on row assignment and already performed these loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold promise can delay hover, but the diff does not add a second network operation because calls share the cached promise/result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Interactive hover frequency and one currently hovered extension row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A per-row `Throttler` serializes/coalesces recomputations for that row; there is no global limiter, but interactive hovering naturally limits simultaneous rows. Status changes can rerender the associated status widget/action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The gallery manifest service memoizes its initialization promise, and `Extension.getGalleryManifest()` memoizes each extension's manifest promise. Initial row status computation already reaches these checks, so hover recomputation normally reads warm caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed recomputation and cache behavior; low evidence of user-visible performance degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Status-pipeline CPU and DOM event cost varies with extension state, but one user hover and warm caches do not establish dropped frames or meaningful latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff adds repeated status CPU/DOM churn, but expensive boundary reads are cached and realistic hover cardinality is bounded; impact is insufficient for a high-confidence performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Computing the Extensions activity badge in delayed mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Runs while deriving the Extensions activity badge after extension state changes; all work is synchronous in memory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single badge recomputation per debounced/change-driven status update; no parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. `isAutoUpdateDelayed` performs configuration/time reads against already materialized extension metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the loop and helper are in-memory only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Outdated lists can vary, but the added constant work per outdated item is trivial relative to the already existing enablement checks and `includes` scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added per-item timestamp/config checks are small in-memory operations with no new I/O or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Periodic plugin marketplace checks and plugin auto-update
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing periodic plugin marketplace checks and silent plugin updates remain on their prior asynchronous paths. The dependency substitution adds no boundary to those paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check plugin marketplace metadata and update installed plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing periodic marketplace request(s) and at most one silent update-all operation per update-available transition; unchanged by the dependency substitution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same periodic and update operations existed; the diff changes which normalized setting values enable them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the foreground UI critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed plugin count per existing periodic cycle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing plugin update code retains its in-flight guard; the PR does not increase aggregate parallelism within a cycle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plugin marketplace/update caches and observables are unchanged. The configuration lookup now delegates to normalized `getAutoUpdateValue`; no new plugin data cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code only replaces direct config reads with the normalized extension-workbench setting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin count and network duration vary, but no changed call cardinality or concurrency was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: existing network/update boundaries retain their frequency and concurrency; any delayed-mode semantic mismatch is correctness-only.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and traced startup migration, policy/context updates, extension enablement, delayed eligibility timers, marketplace polling/install boundaries, hover/status rendering, badge computation, and plugin updates. Submitted two medium findings: default-mode enablement events now launch uncoalesced full-inventory gallery checks, and staggered delayed deadlines repeat full-inventory checks instead of targeted grouped refreshes. No concrete regression was established for startup, cached hover status recomputation, badge filtering, or plugin config delegation.
